transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... I'm just having a really hard time at work. I do bookkeeping, and I just can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. 

It's gotten to the point where I'm staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves. Even when I've already checked the numbers and I know they're right, I just... I feel like I have to do it one more time. Because if I don't check it again, I get this overwhelming feeling that something really bad is going to happen, and it'll be entirely my fault.
Do you have these repetitive thoughts or urges to check things when you're not at work?

Well, it's mostly about work, but the thoughts definitely follow me home. Like, even after I leave the office and I know the numbers match, this thought just keeps jumping in. I'll be at home and suddenly think that I missed one hidden mistake in payroll or the taxes. I start worrying that somebody's check won't go through, or the firm will get in trouble. I try to push the thought away so I can just relax, but it comes right back. It's like... I just can't trust my own eyes.
Do you have similar worries or repetitive thoughts about things outside of work?

No, not really. I mean... I haven't really noticed anything like that. It's pretty much just the bookkeeping stuff. I don't worry about checking things around my apartment or anything like that. It really is just the numbers for my job that I get completely stuck on.
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge when you're not thinking about work?

Not really. I mean... it's hard to find a time when I'm not thinking about work lately, to be honest. But if I actually manage to distract myself and stop thinking about it for a minute, I don't feel anxious just out of nowhere. The on-edge feeling is pretty much always tied to worrying I messed up the numbers. If I'm not thinking about that, I feel pretty normal.
Have you noticed any changes in your body when you're feeling anxious about the numbers, like a racing heart or sweating?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean... my heart doesn't race, and I don't get sweaty or anything. It's really just the thoughts that won't stop. But physically, no, I don't think my body does anything weird when I get like that.
Has this issue with repeatedly checking numbers affected your relationships or other areas of your life outside of work?

Yeah, it really has. I mean, at work, I actually missed a filing deadline recently because of it, and I got called into a formal meeting. And outside of work... I've basically stopped making it to my choir rehearsals and my volunteer commitments at the youth center. I just... I can't get out of the office on time anymore because I'm stuck there checking everything.
How upsetting or disturbing do you find these recurring thoughts about the numbers to be?

It's really upsetting, honestly. Even after I check everything and I know for a fact the numbers match, this thought just keeps jumping into my head that I missed one hidden mistake somewhere in the payroll or the taxes. I start worrying that somebody's check won't go through, or the firm is going to get in serious trouble because of me. I try to just push the thought away and move on, but it comes right back. It's incredibly frustrating because it's like... I just can't trust my own eyes anymore.
Do you feel like you have to perform any specific rituals or behaviors when you're not checking the numbers to try and reduce your anxiety?

No, not really. I don't have any, like, special routines or anything like that. It's really just the checking. If I'm not checking the numbers, I'm just... sitting there worrying about them. But I don't do anything else to try and make it stop.
Do you feel like these thoughts about checking the numbers are coming from your own mind and are something you want to be thinking about?

Well, yeah, I know it's my own brain doing it. It's not like someone else is putting the thoughts there or anything. But I definitely do not want to be thinking about it. If I could just do my job and go home without worrying, I would in a heartbeat. I just... I don't really know why my mind gets stuck on it like this.
Are you feeling like these thoughts and behaviors are taking a toll on your overall well-being or happiness?

Yeah, it really is. It's affecting pretty much everything. I actually... well, I missed a filing deadline recently, and I got called into a formal meeting at work about it. And it's not just work. I've stopped making it to my choir rehearsals, and I can't do my commitments at the youth center anymore either. I just can't get out of the office on time to go to them. So, yeah, it's definitely taking a big toll on my life right now.
Are there any other parts of your life, besides work and the activities you've mentioned, that you feel are being negatively impacted by these thoughts and behaviors?

Um, no, not really. I mean, work and the choir and volunteering at the youth center... that pretty much makes up my whole schedule anyway. I don't really do much else. 

I guess I just go straight home now and kind of crash, mostly because I'm so exhausted from being stressed at the office all day. But as far as other activities or things like that... no, there isn't really anything else specific that comes to mind. It's just mainly the things I already mentioned.
Are you having trouble enjoying time with family or friends because of these thoughts about work?

Um, no, not really. I don't really have a lot of close friends right now anyway, and my family doesn't live nearby. I mean, I guess if I did have plans with people, I'd probably be too tired to go or I'd be late because I was stuck at the office. But since I don't really have those kinds of plans, it hasn't really been an issue.
Are you feeling like you're losing control over your life because of these thoughts and behaviors?

I guess I haven't really thought about it exactly like that. I mean, I don't feel completely out of control, but... I definitely don't feel like I'm the one steering things right now. It's more like I'm just stuck in this loop at work and I can't figure out how to stop it. So maybe a little bit, yeah.
Are there any other ways, besides the impact on your work and the activities you've stopped doing, that you feel your life is being affected by these thoughts and behaviors?

Um, no, I don't think so. Like I said, it's mostly just work and those few activities I used to do. I mean, I guess I'm just really tired all the time from dealing with it, but other than that... no, I can't really think of anything else it's affecting.
Are you feeling like these thoughts and behaviors are significantly interfering with your ability to function in daily life or causing a lot of distress for you?

Yeah, it really is. I mean, it's causing a lot of problems. Like I mentioned with work... it's actually gotten to the point where I missed a filing deadline recently, and I got called into a formal meeting about it. 

And those activities I said I stopped doing? That was my choir rehearsals and my commitments at the youth center. I just... I've stopped making it to them entirely because I literally can't get out of the office on time anymore. So, yeah, it's definitely interfering with everything.
Are there any other areas of your life where you feel like these thoughts and behaviors are causing problems or making it hard for you to function?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, between work and having to drop out of choir and the youth center, that pretty much covers my whole schedule anyway. I mostly just go straight home and sleep after work now because I'm so drained from dealing with it all day. So... yeah, I think that's really everything.
Are you feeling like these thoughts about checking numbers are making it hard for you to enjoy things you used to find pleasurable?

Um, I don't think so. It's not really that I can't enjoy things anymore... I mean, I still really like the idea of going to choir and everything. It's just that I literally don't have the time or energy for it because I'm stuck at the office. So, no, I wouldn't say the thoughts stop me from feeling pleasure or enjoying stuff... I just don't actually get to do those fun things right now.
Are you feeling like these thoughts and behaviors are causing problems in your relationships with others?

Um, no, not really. I don't really think it's affecting my relationships. I mean, I live alone, and like I said, I pretty much just work and then go home and sleep. So... I guess I'm not really seeing anyone enough right now for it to cause problems with them. It's mostly just messing up my own schedule.
Do you think your difficulty with repeatedly checking numbers is causing you more distress than the actual problems it might prevent?

Um, I'm not really sure how to answer that. I mean, the checking definitely causes me a lot of stress... like, I'm exhausted all the time. But at the same time, if I didn't check, and I messed up someone's accounts at work, that would be a huge problem. So... I don't know if it's more distress than what it prevents. I just know I have to do it.
Do you think the anxiety you feel is primarily about the specific task of checking numbers, or is it more of a general feeling of worry that something might go wrong?

Um, I think it's mostly just about the numbers. I don't really walk around worrying about random things going wrong in my life, you know? It's pretty much just... when I'm looking at the accounts at work. That's when the anxiety really hits. So I guess it's just about that specific task. Outside of making sure those spreadsheets are exactly right, I don't really have a general feeling of worry about everything else.
